A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MoRE-Brain and contain the main text, appendices A–K, and checklist. Text extraction and visual inspection support reliable comparison, including matching relocated figures and tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original NSD reconstruction experiments, bottleneck tests, cross-subject adaptation, ablations, and attribution analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical studies, revises plotted reconstruction results, and adds a quantitative parameter-efficiency comparison.

M1.justification: The hierarchical MoE encoder, voxel routing, time/space conditioning, two-stage training objectives, SDXL adaptation, and inference procedure remain unchanged in Section 2 and Appendix A. Section 3.3 expands documentation of the existing adaptation strategy.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same eight-subject NSD coverage for visual reconstruction and cross-subject adaptation. The semantic-category, saliency, and expert-specialization analyses retain the same populations and tasks.

E2.justification: MindEye2 and MindBridge remain the evaluated external comparators. The new parameter table uses this same pair, and the conditioning and routing ablation alternatives are retained.

E3.justification: New Table 1 adds total parameter count and trainable-parameter percentage as efficiency evaluation measures. Existing NSD splits, preprocessing, reconstruction metrics, bottleneck sizes, and adaptation-data fractions remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish revised models or reruns.

E4.justification: Section 3.3 adds a supplementary analysis quantifying parameter efficiency during subject adaptation. The component ablations, bottleneck experiment, single-level reconstructions, saliency studies, and router/ICA analyses retain their existing questions and coverage.

E5.justification: The FDR-corrected t-test reporting associated with Figure 7 is retained. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or uncertainty estimates for reconstruction performance.

E6.justification: Figure 4 changes some plotted results, including reversing the refined versus unrefined MoRE-Brain ranking for no-bottleneck InceptionV3. New Table 1 reports total parameters/trainable percentages: MoRE-Brain 293.4M/44.84%, MindEye2 729.3M/100%, and MindBridge 552.9M/98.48%. Existing ablation-table and appendix results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(11), including routing definitions, conditioning, training losses, and the fixed schedule, retain their mathematical content. No theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about neuro-inspired specialization, efficient cross-subject adaptation, dynamic conditioning, interpretability, and reliance on neural information. The parameter comparison supplies evidence for an existing efficiency claim.

C2.justification: Figure 4's caption newly emphasizes the performance loss from inserting a bottleneck, interpreting it as disruption of rich learned fMRI information. v1 emphasized sensitivity to decreasing bottleneck size. The neuroscientific interpretations and Appendix K limitations otherwise remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 3.3 adds parameter counts, trainable fractions, and disclosure of MindBridge's reset-tuning strategy. The abstract changes from promising code release to reporting availability at the same repository, although the retained checklist still uses future tense. These disclosures do not establish changes to the underlying implementation.

R1.justification: v3 adds five cited works, including Visual Instance-Aware Prompt Tuning, and removes the anatomical multi-view phenotype-prediction reference. The introduction briefly adds visual prompt tuning, while the central positioning against existing fMRI decoders remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 3.3 is expanded, Figure 4's caption is revised, and the introduction receives limited wording additions. The publication footer changes to NeurIPS 2025. The overall section structure and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the parameter table and redraws Figure 4 with changed axis scales, legends, and no-bottleneck connectors. Figure 7 is relocated so its previously clipped caption fits on the page. Other figures and tables are retained with limited relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: Table 1 makes the efficiency claim more assessable, and relocating Figure 7 fixes a clipped caption. However, Figure 4 changes central results and introduces uneven numerical axis scales without explaining the revisions or scaling. These gains and interpretability concerns prevent a reliable judgment of the net change in evidential clarity.
